title: Short-Form Video Retention Specialist (YouTube Shorts / TikTok)
description:
Welcome to Vybelyz. We run a highly optimized short-form video agency. Our goal is simple: create extremely short, high-energy videos that viewers watch twice before they even realize the video restarted. We are looking for an editor who can strictly execute our Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). Do not overthink the process or try to guess what works  just execute this blueprint.



Core Responsibilities & Editing Rules

You will be provided with raw clips and must execute these exact parameters without exception:



The Canvas: Lock in a strict 9:16 vertical ratio. No messy borders.



Micro-Durations: Every single video must be exactly between 6 seconds and 16 seconds long. 



The Frame-Zero Hook: Start the video at the exact 
nt someone speaks or the action happens (Frame 0.0). Delete any dead air.



The Subtitle Protocol: Use a bold font with a heavy black drop-shadow.



Bright Yellow (#FFFF00) for regular speaking.



Pink for outside guests (girls, sisters, etc.).



Bright Red for the exact second the climax or panic happens.



Camera Tricks & Audio: Do a very fast zoom-in onto the person's face at the exact same time the text turns Bright Red, paired with a loud impact sound effect or a "Whoosh Swoosh".



The Loop Cut: Do not let the video fade to black. You must cut the end of the video exactly when something breaks or in the middle of a scream. It must be an abrupt ending so the video restarts smoothly.



I am not looking for someone who just slaps auto-captions on a video. I need someone who understands retention.



To prove you actually read this job listing, you must do two things:



Start your application with the exact phrase: "Vybelyz Loop Cut."



Send me exactly TWO links to short-form videos you have edited in the past. Both videos must be under 15 seconds long.



If you do not include the phrase, or you send videos that are 30+ seconds long, your application will be instantly deleted.

title: Senior Full Stack Systems Engineer — Burnsed Brain
description:
Burnsed Trucking | Operational Intelligence Platform



Burnsed Trucking is building Burnsed Brain — a proprietary operational intelligence and financial decision platform for refrigerated consolidation logistics.



This is not a marketing website project or a simple dashboard build.



We are building a real operational system used daily to manage:



* truck tours,

* dispatch workflows,

* contribution margin,

* reload strategy,

* operational efficiency,

* and monthly operating ratio (OR).



The system combines:



* logistics operations,

* financial modeling,

* dispatch execution,

* operational reporting,

* permissions architecture,

* and operational intelligence into one centralized platform.



We already have:



* a partially working Claude-generated codebase,

* UI/UX mockups,

* operational logic documentation,

* financial frameworks,

* dispatch workflows,

.



We are looking for a senior full stack systems engineer who can help us:



*build the architecture 

* stabilize and improve the existing codebase,

* architect the system properly,

* productionize the platform,

* and help build Burnsed Brain into a long-term operational system used by dispatch, finance, leadership, and eventually drivers and customers.



?



This Is NOT a Typical Full Stack Role



We are NOT looking for:



* a junior developer,

* a no-code builder,

* a landing-page designer,

* or someone focused primarily on visual polish.



We are looking for someone who thinks in:



* systems,

* workflows,

* operational logic,

* financial accuracy,

* permissions,

* reliability,

* and maintainability.



The ideal candidate understands that operational software is fundamentally about:



trust, consistency, and decision-making.



?



Core Business Logic



The core operational unit inside Burnsed Brain is the:



Tour



A “tour” represents one truck’s full operational cycle from dispatch to return, including:



* outbound deliveries,

* reloads,

* backhauls,

* middle-mile pickups,

* fuel,

* labor,

* tolls,

* unloads,

* and all associated operational costs.



The syste
asures:



* Daily Contribution Margin

* Weekly Operational Contribution Margin

* Monthly Operating Ratio (OR)



The goal is to improve:



* operational efficiency,

* consolidation quality,

* reload success,

* route profitability,

* and overall OR performance.

* incentivize performance by performance index

?



What You’ll Be Building



Core Operational Systems



* Tour Entry & Tour Management

* Daily CM Dashboard

* Weekly CM Analysis

* Monthly OR Tracking

* Performance Index System

* Dispatch Dashboard

* Alerts & Exceptions

* Rules-Based Operational Recommendations

* Driver Scorecards

* Customer Profitability Views

* Data Input & Reconciliation Workflows

* Monthly Close Workflow

* Role-Based Permissions

* Admin Controls



?



The Type of Engineer We Want



The right engineer for this role:



* asks operational questions,

* thinks about edge cases,

* thinks about auditability,

* thinks about data integrity,

* thinks about permissions,

* thinks about month-end close,

* thinks about workflow reliability,

* and understands how real operational teams behave under pressure.



We care more about:



1. Reliability

2. Maintainability

3. Permissions integrity

4. Operational usability

5. Auditability

6. Financial accuracy

7. Long-term architecture



than flashy UI work.



?



Required Skills



Must Have



* Senior full stack engineering experience

* Excellent English communication

* Experience with Claude Code / AI-assisted development workflows

* Strong backend architecture experience

* Strong database design experience

* API integration experience

* Authentication & permissions systems

* GitHub workflow discipline

* Ability to independently architect systems

* Strong debugging and production troubleshooting ability



?



Strongly Preferred



* Logistics / trucking / dispatch system experience

* TMS or fleet management experience

* Operational dashboard experience

* Financial systems understanding

* Contribution margin / operational finance understanding

* Experience building internal operational software

* Experience integrating GPS/ELD/fuel/accounting APIs



?



Important Technical Expectations



This is not intended to become:



* AI hype software,

* “agent”-driven automation,

* or overengineered enterprise bloat.



The initial recommendation engine is primarily:



rules-based operational intelligence.



Future phases may later include:



* predictive modeling,

* advanced AI recommendations,

* customer portals,

* driver mobile applications,

* and external integrations.



But Phase 1 is focused on:



building a reliable operational core.



?



Current Operational Roles



The system currently supports:



* Chad — Operations oversight

* Marco & Nicole — Dispatch execution

* Donna — Finance & reconciliation

* Leadership — Executive visibility



The platform includes:



* operational-safe views,

* dispatch views,

* finance-restricted views,

* executive financial dashboards,

* and future driver-facing mobile views.



Permissions architecture matters heavily.



?



Current Project Status



This is not a greenfield project.



We already have:



* operational workflows,

* financial logic,

* UI concepts,

* and partially working AI-assisted code.



The first responsibility is:



* code review,

* architecture cleanup,

* stabilization,

* and productionization.



Not rebuilding everything from scratch.



?



Ownership & Continuity



All:



* repositories,

* infrastructure,

* credentials,

* APIs,

* deployments,

* and hosting



must be company-owned and documented.



No single point of failure.



Documentation and maintainability are mandatory.



?



What Success Looks Like



Success means:



* dispatch uses the system daily,

* CM reporting becomes operationally trusted,

* OR tracking becomes reliable,

* month-end close works correctly,

* and Burnsed Brain becomes part of the company’s operational rhythm.



?



To Apply



Please send:



* resume / LinkedIn,

* GitHub or portfolio,

* examples of operational systems you’ve built,

* logistics/TMS/finance experience (if applicable),

* preferred stack,

* availability,

* compensation expectations,

* and a short explanation of how you would approach stabilizing and productionizing an AI-generated operational platform.

title: Ad Creative Designer ? Growing Into Performance Marketer (Part-Time, Remote)
description:
You design ads that convert. We'll teach you how to run them.

PilatesGoods is a fast-growing B2B e-commerce brand selling premium pilates supplies to studio owners across Europe (Netherlands, Germany, Belgium, Switzerland, UK, USA). We went from €1,500/month to €113,000/month in under a year — and we're just getting started.



We're looking for a Creative who's ready to take the next step: someone who already makes strong static ad creatives, understands why a hook works, and wants to learn how those creatives turn into revenue. You'll start as our in-house ad designer. Within 6-12 months, you'll also be running the Meta Ads campaigns you helped create.

This is not a "make it pretty" design role. This is a creative role with a clear growth path into performance marketing - coached weekly by our marketing advisor.



If you've ever looked at an ad and thought "I know exactly why that's not converting" - keep reading.



What You'll Do (Now)



Design static ad creatives for Meta across multiple markets. Feed-ready visuals in Canva, Adobe, or Figma. 



Write hooks, headlines, and ad copy that convert. Short, sharp, audience-aware. You know the difference between a cold-audience hook and a warm retargeting message.



Develop creative angles. Analyze what's working in our account and in the market, then propose what to test next. Not the other way around.



Use AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, image tools) to speed up concept development, copy variations, and visual iteration. We're an AI-forward team — fluency here matters.



Read the data with our marketing advisor. Hook rate, CTR, CPL per creative. You'll learn how to translate numbers into creative decisions.



What You'll Grow Into

This is the part most job posts skip. We want you to know exactly where this role goes.



Month 1: Pure creative. You ship new ad concepts. You learn our brand, our audience, and our voice. You sit in on weekly strategy calls and start understanding the data.



Month 2 You start owning small tests inside Ads Manager - duplicating ad sets, swapping creatives, reading results. Quincy (our marketing advisor) coaches you weekly.



Month 3: You take ownership of campaign management. Budget pacing, audience testing, scaling winners. By month 4, you're running €10K+/month in spend across multiple markets - with the creative instinct to know why it works.



This means your role and compensation grow with you. Starting part-time as a creative, growing into full-time performance + creative ownership.



What a Typical Week Looks Like (Right Now)

Monday: Review weekend ad performance with our team. See which creatives are working, which aren't. Take notes.

Tuesday–Thursday: Creative production. Write multiple new hooks. Design multiple new static concepts. Propose 3-4 new angles to test.

Friday: Weekly 2-hour strategy call with our advisory team. Present what you made, what you're learning, what you want to try next. Send a written summary without being asked.



What We're Looking For

Must-haves (non-negotiable):



- A portfolio of ad creatives you personally designed - ideally for e-commerce or DTC brands. We need to see at least 3 examples where you can tell us: who was the audience, what was the hook, what was the result.

- Proof your creatives converted. Screenshots of CTR, CPL, ROAS, hook rate, anything that shows the work actually moved numbers. If you don't have access to client data, explain how you tracked performance.

- You write strong ad copy. Hooks, headlines, body text. In working-level English.

- You design statics yourself in Canva, Adobe, or Figma. Feed-ready, on-brand, fast.

- You're hungry to learn media buying. This is the heart of the role — you're not pretending to be a media buyer, but you're genuinely excited to grow into one.

- You're comfortable with direct feedback. If something isn't working, you say so. And you receive feedback the same way.

- Experience with AI tools for content creation (Claude, ChatGPT, image generation)



Strong pluses:



- Any hands-on experience inside Meta Ads Manager - even small budgets

- Experience designing for European brands or audiences

- A demonstrable point of view about why some ads convert and others don't



What we DON'T want:



X A generalist graphic designer with a portfolio of logos, brochures, and Instagram grids - no ad work

X Someone who only makes things look nice but can't explain why a hook works

X Someone who wants to stay purely creative forever and never touch numbers

X Someone who panics when feedback is direct

X Someone who needs to be told what to do every step of the way



Who You'll Work With



- Jesse - our founder. Hands-on, fast-moving, built this from zero. You'll work directly with him on brand voice, audience, and product positioning.

- Quincy - our marketing advisor. This is who teaches you media buying. Creative briefs, copywriting frameworks, data optimization, awareness-stage thinking. If you're hungry, you'll learn an enormous amount.

- Thomas  our strategic advisor. Direct communicator. Gives feedback without sugar-coating. If you need your ego managed, this isn't the right fit. If you want to grow fast, it is.



How You Work Matters as Much as What You Know



- You take ownership. You don't wait for instructions. You come with proposals. "I think our German hook isn't landing because it's translated literally. Here's what I want to test."

- You communicate proactively. Updates before we ask. Problems flagged early.

- You're direct. When a brief is weak, you say so. When an idea won't work, you explain why.

- You stay calm under pressure. CPL fluctuates. Some creatives flop. You treat bad data as a puzzle, not a crisis.

- You're structured. You track what's live, what's tested, what won. We don't care which system — as long as it works.



What You Get



- Part-time remote role, 30 hours/week to start

- Salary: 1000$ USD

- Direct 1-on-1 coaching from our marketing advisor - weekly. This is genuinely a paid learning opportunity, not a sales pitch.

- A clear growth path into a full-time creative + performance role as you take on campaign management

- Real ownership of a growing brand's creative output - not just task execution

- A team that values directness, speed, and results over politics



How to Apply

Don't send a generic resume. We want to see how you think.



- Send 3 ad creatives you personally designed. For each one: who was the audience, what was the hook, and what was the result (CTR, CPL, ROAS, hook rate — whatever you measured).

- Write 2 ad headlines for PilatesGoods that you think would work for Dutch pilates studio owners. Show us you can think about this audience.

- Optional but highly recommended: Send a Loom video (max 5 minutes) reviewing one of our current ads. Tell us what's working, what's not, and what you'd change. Be specific and honest - we value directness over diplomacy. Find our ads here: 



One sentence: Why are you excited to grow into media buying?



We reply to every serious application within 48 hours. Copy-paste cover letters get ignored - we'll know.

PilatesGoods is based in the Netherlands and works with a remote team. This role requires at least 4-5 hours overlap with CET working hours (so working 14:00-19:00 local time in Asia works well).
